challenges.finding: Contact follow-up is 68.6% in Tshopo amid a health-worker strike and aggression against response teams; Wamba reports 63.3%. Butuhe remains closed; Haut-Uele and Bas-Uele report connectivity and transport constraints.

Ituri reports 40 critical patients and a continuing blood stockout. Nord-Kivu reports 19 critical patients and 188 outside CTE/CT. Two confirmed patients remain missing after leaving Bafwasende. Bas-Uele has no functional CTE or nutritional support for 38 isolated suspects.

Nord-Kivu reports no kits for six decontaminated households, eight unopened rings and 40 postponed safe burials. Bas-Uele reports 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage; a strike disrupts Buta, Ganga and Viadana. Haut-Uele reports only four of seven zones and shortages of IPC kits.

Ituri reports 112 vaccinated during the day and 2,081 cumulatively in ongoing research activities; this report does not establish BDBV vaccine efficacy. No Bas-Uele vaccination data were transmitted. Bas-Uele UCC remain inactive and vaccine supply is insufficient.

Tshopo assessments of Bethanie and Maison Medicale report ineffective triage and a second-line tuberculosis drug stockout. In Nord-Kivu, Maboya and Matanda lack emergency services and absenteeism contingency plans; three of 27 staff were trained in IPC. Four provinces did not transmit continuity data.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 15 of 28 affected zones. Ten affected Nord-Kivu zones lack nurseries. Wanie-Rukula teams lack training, communications and mobility; Bas-Uele psychosocial support for confirmed cases is delayed. Pillar cohorts differ from daily incidence.

Tshopo reports 115 motorcycles missing and a second-line tuberculosis drug stockout. Bas-Uele Buta treatment-centre construction is 50% complete; diesel, computers, printers and scanners are missing. Security threats persist against response teams.

Only three of eight provincial directorates reported PSEA activities. The reporting mechanism is known in six of 34 Nord-Kivu zones. Haut-Uele lacks sensitisation tools; the community complaints mechanism is incomplete in Kisangani zones.

priorities: Strengthen early detection, contact follow-up and safe burials; source recommendation, not completion.
